questions.question: Who invaded India during the rule of Tughlaq Dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Timur's Invasion (1398): Timur
  • Context: He invaded during the reign of Nasir-ud-din Mahmud Shah Tughluq, effectively ending the Tughlaq power.

questions.question: Where is the Kailasa temple built by Rashtrakutas located?
questions.solution:
• Kailasha Temple: Ellora
  • Architecture: A massive rock-cut Hindu temple built by the Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.

questions.question: ‘The Life Divine’, ‘The Synthesis of Yoga’ and ‘Savitri’ are the popular works of which of the following extremist freedom fighters of India?
questions.solution:
• Aurobindo Ghosh Works: Aurobindo Ghosh
  • Evolution: He transitioned from a revolutionary extremist to a prominent spiritual philosopher.

questions.question: Which Mughal ruler was responsible for the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur in the year 1675?
questions.solution:
• Guru Tegh Bahadur: Aurangzeb
  • History: The 9th Sikh Guru was executed in Chandni Chowk, Delhi, for refusing to convert to Islam.

questions.question: In which year did Swami Vivekananda give his speech at the Chicago Parliament of Religions?
questions.solution:
• Chicago Speech: 1893
  • Impact: This speech introduced Vedantic and Yoga philosophies to the Western world.

questions.question: Which Commission drew the boundary line between India and Pakistan?
questions.solution:
• Radcliffe Line: Radcliffe Boundary Commission
  • Partition: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the commission that partitioned Bengal and Punjab in 1947.

questions.question: The Battle of Khanua was fought between Babur and ________.
questions.solution:
• Battle of Khanua (1527): Rana Sanga
  • Significance: Babur used the 'Jihad' slogan and superior artillery to defeat the Rajput confederacy.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I- Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay.

II- All India Radio came into being in 1936.

III - In 1976, TV was delinked from All India Radio (AIR) and got a separate identity as Door darshan (DD).
questions.option_1: Both I and II are correct.
questions.option_2: I, II and III are correct
questions.option_4: Both II and III are correct.
questions.solution:
• Media History: I, II and III are correct
  • Detail: TV was originally part of AIR but became 'Doordarshan' in 1976.

questions.question: Which organisation was started in the Pune district of Maharashtra in the 1870s with the aim of promoting education and social rights among the underprivileged group of the society?
questions.solution:
• Satyashodhak Samaj: Satyashodhak Samaj
  • Founder: Jyotirao Phule (1873). Its goal was to liberate Shudras and Dalits from exploitation.

questions.question: What is the name of the famous British social reformer known for founding the Indian Home Rule League in 1916?
questions.solution:
• Annie Besant: Annie Besant
  • Movement: She founded the Home Rule League in Madras, while Tilak founded his in Pune.

questions.question: Who was the Indian Buddhist monk who is credited with the development of many ancient martial art forms in the 5th century?
questions.solution:
• Bodhidharma: Bodhidharma
  • Legend: A monk from Kanchipuram credited with carrying the Zen (Chan) school of Buddhism and martial arts to China.

questions.question: The Sun Temple at Konark was built under the rule of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Konark Sun Temple: Eastern Ganga Dynasty
  • Builder: King Narasimhadeva I (13th century). It is designed as a chariot with 24 wheels.

questions.question: Which British colonel is remembered as the Butcher of Amritsar for his role in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919?
questions.solution:
• General Dyer: Reginald Dyer
  • 1919: He ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar.

questions.question: From which book is the national song of India compiled?
questions.solution:
• Anand Math: Anand Math
  • National Song: 'Vande Mataram' is taken from this novel by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

questions.question: Who amongst the following Delhi Sultanate rulers sent his army under Malik Kafur’s command to conquer South India?
questions.solution:
• Malik Kafur's Campaign: Alauddin Khilji
  • Expedition: Kafur (a eunuch general) reached as far south as Madurai, raiding the Hoysalas and Pandyas.

questions.question: Which type of system did the leaders of independent India decide to adopt?
questions.option_1: A system that would promote the welfare of all rather than a few
questions.option_2: A system that would promote the welfare of the government
questions.option_3: A system that would promote the welfare of private enterprises
questions.option_4: A system that would promote the welfare of few rather than all
questions.solution:
• Independent India's Goal: A system that would promote the welfare of all rather than a few
  • Constitution: This aligns with the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution.
